title: The Turkey Board
trend: TikTok 'Turkey Charcuterie Boards' (time-lapse builds of cheese, crackers and meat arranged as a turkey; New Engen TikTok list, updated Nov 13 2026, US) + Friendsgiving weekend — Aunt Dolores builds a turkey-shaped snack board for tonight while her husband Lou and nephew Benny keep eating the feathers and the cheese ball body narrates; twist: the board was a decoy built from the dog's biscuits, because they have eaten her board every year since nineteen ninety eight, and the real one is hidden in the garage fridge
youtube_title: Aunt Dolores built a turkey out of snacks. It did not survive the afternoon 🦃
description:
Aunt Dolores spent all morning building a turkey out of cheese and crackers for tonight. Uncle Lou calls it quality control. The cheese ball knows the truth.

#cartoon #animation #funny #thanksgiving #shorts
tiktok_caption: aunt dolores built a turkey out of snacks 🦃 #cartoon #animation #funny #thanksgiving

lines.text: Friendsgiving is tonight. And this year I am building a turkey. Out of snacks.
I am the body. I was told there would be a lot of respect.
Salami folded into little fans. Those are the feathers.
Crackers in between. Grapes for the eyes. Pretzels for the feet.
It is beautiful. I have never felt so seen.
Nobody touches it until six o'clock. Nobody.
Morning, Dolly. Whoa. Look at this bird.
Don't. Look with your eyes, Louis.
I'm just checking the feathers. For quality.
He has eaten a feather. The turkey now has eleven feathers.
Quality is good. Very good.
Lou. That was a feather.
Turkeys lose feathers, Dolly. It's nature.
Aunt Dolores! Is that a turkey? Made of food?
Benny, baby, it is for tonight. Hands in your pockets.
I just want to say hi to it.
He said hi to the eyes. The eyes are gone.
They were grapes. They were looking at me.
Now the turkey cannot see. It has to trust me.
I will put in new eyes. Olives. Very serious olives.
Now it looks worried.
It is worried. I am also worried.
Okay. I am going to shower. Nobody move.
We would never.
We would never times two.
Ten minutes later.
The feet are gone. The turkey is floating now.
Pretzels go bad, Benny. We had to.
Pretzels do not go bad, Uncle Lou.
Not anymore they don't.
Six feathers left. It looks less like a turkey and more like a sad hand.
We can fix it. We just spread the feathers out.
Spread them out. Like a turkey with a lot of space.
Do not even look at me. I am the body. I am structural.
Just a little corner.
A ball has no corners, Louis. That is the whole idea of a ball.
I'm back. What happened to my turkey?
It flew away, Dolly. They do that.
Most of it flew into Uncle Lou.
Benny took the eyes.
Every year since nineteen ninety eight, you two eat my board.
That is why I made two.
Two?
The real turkey is in the garage fridge. Behind the paint cans. With a lock.
We have a lock?
We have a lock, Louis. I bought it in nineteen ninety eight.
So this one was a fake turkey?
This was the decoy. And those crackers were not crackers.
What were they?
The dog's biscuits. Peanut butter flavor.
I ate nine of those.
They were the best part.
And now you know why the dog has such a shiny coat.
I do feel shiny.
Tonight you both sit at the far end of the table.
Next to the turkey?
Next to the dog. He wants his biscuits back.
For the record, I am not even cheese. I am a candle shaped like a cheese ball.
She bought me in nineteen ninety eight. I have been the decoy every year since.
Since ninety eight?
Stop looking at me like that, Louis. I am a candle.
